definitions.gloss: one's own handwriting; written by one's own hand
definitions.explanation: Something written personally by hand, as opposed to being typed, printed, or written by someone else. Emphasizes authenticity and personal authorship.

examples.japanese: これは{作者|さくしゃ}の{自筆|じひつ}の{原稿|げんこう}です。
examples.english: This is the author's handwritten manuscript.

examples.japanese: {自筆|じひつ}の{手紙|てがみ}には{特別|とくべつ}な{温|あたた}かみがある。
examples.english: A handwritten letter has a special warmth to it.

examples.japanese: {遺言書|ゆいごんしょ}は{自筆|じひつ}で{書|か}かなければ{法的|ほうてき}に{有効|ゆうこう}にならない{場合|ばあい}がある。
examples.english: In some cases, a will must be written in one's own hand to be legally valid.

notes:
A compound of {自|じ} (self) and {筆|ひつ} (brush, writing). Used as a noun modifier: {自筆|じひつ}の{手紙|てがみ} (handwritten letter).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自筆|じひつ}の{手紙|てがみ} (handwritten letter)
- {自筆|じひつ}の{原稿|げんこう} (handwritten manuscript)
- {自筆|じひつ}{証書|しょうしょ}{遺言|ゆいごん} (holographic will — a legal term)
- {自筆|じひつ}で{書|か}く (to write in one's own hand)
- {自筆|じひつ}サイン (personal autograph/signature)

In legal contexts, {自筆|じひつ}{証書|しょうしょ}{遺言|ゆいごん} refers to a will written entirely by the testator's own hand, which has specific legal requirements in Japanese law.
